search_agent_plugin_local.description: Find an Agent Plugin by the task, capability, skill or MCP server you need. Searches local agent-plugins.org packages (plugin.json, skills and optional mcp.json) in this workspace, including inactive packages. For the full plugin inventory, use content_read.plugin. Empty, omitted or whitespace query returns every local Agent Plugin in plugin-id order, including enabled status. Nonblank queries return ranked matches. Results are byte-bounded: id, pluginId, enabled, maturity when declared, and a short description. plugins_set_enabled with family 'agent-plugin' changes enabled status. An installed, off result is only a catalog entry. Offer its enable card, then read its guidance before connecting or requesting credentials; never guess its sign-in method. Local packages only — never a marketplace or the web. Once you have the right id, call load_agent_plugin({ pluginId }) for that plugin's full guidance. Page with the returned nextOffset as offset, keeping query and limit unchanged. A result with maturity 'soon' isn't ready and can't be turned on: never offer to enable, connect or use it; you may say it's coming soon. Batch: to do several at once, pass items: [{...}, ...] (up to 25) in ONE call instead of one call per item. Canonical shape: {items:[{...}, ...]} only. Legacy shared top-level fields are normalized into each item; item values win. Returns { batch: true, outcome: completed | partial_failure | error, total, succeeded, failed, results: [{ index, ok, result | error }] }; one item's failure does not stop the others.

query.description: What you're looking for, in plain language — e.g. 'a plugin for deploying a server app', 'accessibility guidance', 'gdpr compliance checks'. Matched against each installed Agent Plugin's id, author-declared keywords, description, and bundled skills. Optional; empty, omitted or whitespace lists all installed plugins.

offset.description: Zero-based result offset. Start at 0; continue with nextOffset until null.

limit.description: Max results to return (1-50). Optional, defaults to 10.

items.description: Batch: up to 25 inputs run in ONE call, in order. Each item takes the same fields as a single call; Canonical shape: {items:[{...}, ...]} only. Legacy shared top-level fields are normalized into each item before execution; an item's own value wins.

credential_save.description: Save, add, connect or rotate a credential through a secure human form. The person types the API key, token or password in a masked card; it is sealed server-side and never enters chat or model input. This one call waits for submit, cancel, expiry or abandonment. Choose kind: api for any third-party API, such as a payments or email API, DNS registrar or hosting API; media-provider for image/video generation keys; source-control for git repository commit and backup tokens; publish-host for static site hosting or object storage credentials; agent-plugin-token for an installed plugin personal access token fallback after agent_plugin_connect could not start OAuth sign-in; provider-settings to show a provider plugin’s manifest settings card (target is the pluginId from provider_status); plugin-provider for a provider whose installed plugin ships its own key card, which asks for the key and required public connection fields and saves through that domain’s existing owner. Prefer a plugin-declared card whenever one covers the task. Examples: create an API credential with {kind:"api",label:"payments",baseUrl:"https://api.example.test",category:"general"}; rotate a saved API token with {kind:"api",target:"hosting-prod"} (target is the exact saved label, username is preserved); save an image generation key with {kind:"media-provider",target:"image-provider"}; connect repository backups with {kind:"source-control",target:"<repository provider id>",label:"default"}; save a hosting connection with {kind:"publish-host",target:"<storage provider id>",prefill:{bucket:"my-site",region:"us-east-1"}}; use a plugin token with {kind:"agent-plugin-token",target:"<plugin id>"}; open a plugin’s own key card with {kind:"plugin-provider",target:"<provider id>"}. Discover targets first with content_read.custom_credential, media_list_providers, source_control_get_capabilities or deployment_get_static_publish_capabilities. Choose the card or saved key whose usedFor covers the task; do not ask the person. usedFor is display text, not permission or verification. API creation accepts optional label/baseUrl/category/worksFor prefill; without target it creates a new row and refuses a duplicate label. Publish prefill accepts only provider-declared non-secret fields. Never supply a secret in any argument. Before opening any key card, explain which service and purpose it is for. Refuse to open a replacement-token card for a saved working credential unless the person explicitly asked to replace that key. When explicitly asked to show provider settings, open kind provider-settings; opening the card does not save anything until the person submits. Never open secret-entry cards during a read-only request or to answer what a token is. Read saved metadata and answer in words first. Account-management access may require a separate plugin connection; do not overwrite a working sending key to obtain broader access. Permissions stay per kind: custom-credentials.write, admin.integrations.manage (media/plugin), source-control.credentials.write, deployments.credentials.write, admin.plugins.enable (provider-settings). Results retain each kind’s safe save status and errors; only API creation returns created/credential. Saving a media key does not verify it or add adapter support. External MCP server config, user creation, database destinations and app environment secrets use their own action tools. Saving a project key on a card attaches it to this site. After success retry the original request once.

target.description: Existing API credential label to rotate, media/source-control/publish/plugin provider id, or installed plugin id.

label.description: Optional new API or source-control credential label; never a secret.

baseUrl.description: API creation only: non-secret base URL prefill.

worksFor.description: API creation only: explicit host or vendor IDs to preselect in the secure form.

reason.description: Media only: non-secret reason shown on the form.

prefill.description: Publish only: provider-declared non-secret credential fields. Never tokens, keys or passwords.

agent_plugin_connect.description: Connects an installed Agent Plugin's account by walking the human through its sign-in, then waits until it is done. Call this once you know which plugin needs connecting (e.g. from search_agent_plugin_local, whose result names a MCP server that is not yet connected) — it needs no prior setup, this provisions the connection itself the first time it is called for a given plugin. Token-only plugins reuse a saved credential or show their secure key card. They return connected only after a save succeeds; cancelled, expired or failed cards return not-connected with reason. OAuth plugins attempt sign-in first; only a successful start shows the human a card with a sign-in link and parks until they finish. Do not promise a card before it is emitted. If sign-in fails, explain that no card opened and use the plugin's declared credential_save key card when available. Never ask the person to restart Tovu. Returns { status: 'connected' } once the sign-in completes, or { status: 'waiting-for-sign-in' } if nobody finished within a few minutes — call this again with the same pluginId once the human says they're back; never loop on your own. For a plugin that declares its own API connection, the result also carries connectionRef: pass it unchanged as connectionRef to that plugin's tools (it is an opaque reference, not a secret, and works only for that plugin). Never returns a token, a URL, or any row id — only safe status, outcome guidance and that connectionRef. Refused with a plain error if the plugin has no supported connection, more than one token server, or more than one still-unconnected OAuth server (connect those one at a time).

agent_plugin_ui_ux_design.description: Load guidance to use or apply this plugin before making any design/implementation decision in its domain — Ui Ux Design guidance from the installed 'ui-ux-design' Agent Plugin, covering 2 skills: Frontend Accessibility (frontend-accessibility) — Use when checking accessible controls. | Ui Ux Design (ui-ux-design) — Use when defining visual foundations. Called with no argument, returns this plugin's own eponymous 'ui-ux-design' skill. Pass the optional 'skill' argument to request a different one by name. Pass optional 'file' (for example 'references/foundations.md') relative to the chosen skill folder to read supporting text instead of SKILL.md. Every response lists readable supporting files and other skills with short descriptions; unknown or refused files return a recovery note. For viewing this plugin's admin screen, use page.navigate with its entity target, then discover and click its details handle. Plugin discovery: unknown/ui-ux-design.

file.description: Optional supporting text file relative to the chosen skill folder, e.g. references/foundations.md. Omit to read SKILL.md. Use paths from files in the previous result. Unknown, unsafe, binary or over-256-KiB files return a note and valid files.

skill.description: Optional. Request one specific skill's full guidance instead of the default overview. One of: frontend-accessibility, ui-ux-design. Defaults to 'ui-ux-design' when omitted; an unrecognized value falls back to that same default and reports the valid values instead of failing.

agent_plugin_ui_ux_design__memory_read.description: Read ui-ux-design's learned account knowledge. UTF-8 text only. Never credentials or permissions. Omit entryPath to list learned entries. A missing entry returns exists:false.
